docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Documentation lives in the docs/ folder of each repository. To update a repo's docs:

  1. Edit the Markdown files in docs/
  2. Commit and push to main
  3. This site will automatically update within a few minutes

New to Git/GitHub? Start with the Glossary for plain-language explanations of terms like repo, commit, and pull request.

Refer to the repo-template repository for guidance on structure and workflows.

docs.title: How to Add Your Repository
docs.text: Every repository in the GitHEE-UMCU organization can contribute its documentation to this site. Here's how.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create your repo from the template
docs.text: When creating a new GitHub repository, select repo-template as the template. This gives you the correct folder structure and automated workflows out of the box.

docs.title: Step 2 — Fill out repo-manifest.yml
docs.text:
Open docs/repo-manifest.yml in your repo and fill in the fields:

Field What to write name Short human-readable name description One sentence: what the repo does analysis_type Pick from the list below methods Pick from the list below language R, Python, Stata, Excel, or mixed contact Your name or email status active, archived, or prototype

docs.title: Allowed values
docs.text:
analysis_type

Value Meaning cost-effectiveness Economic evaluation comparing costs and outcomes budget-impact Estimating financial impact of a policy or intervention burden-of-disease Quantifying disease prevalence, incidence, or impact epidemiology Studying disease distribution and determinants literature-review Systematic or narrative review of existing evidence data-pipeline Cleaning, linking, or transforming data utility Reusable functions, tools, or templates

methods

Value Meaning markov State-transition Markov model decision-tree Decision tree / decision analytic model survival Survival or time-to-event analysis regression Regression modelling (any type) descriptive Descriptive statistics or reporting other Anything else

docs.title: Step 3 — Write docs/index.md
docs.text:
This file becomes the landing page for your repo on this site. A template is already provided when you create from repo-template.

If you skip this step, your README.md is used as a fallback.

docs.title: How updates work
docs.text:
Push to main — the site updates automatically within a few minutes. No manual steps needed.

The workflow triggers on changes to:

  • README.md
  • docs/** (includes docs/repo-manifest.yml)

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Plain-language explanations of the Git/GitHub terms you'll run into around this site and the org's repos. No prior Git experience assumed.

Term What it means Repository (repo) A project's folder, plus its full history of changes. Every analysis, model, or tool in the org lives in its own repo. GitHub The website that hosts all our repos online, so the group can share and collaborate on code. Git The underlying tool that tracks changes to files over time. GitHub is a website built around Git. Clone Downloading a full copy of a repo (history included) onto your own computer. Commit A saved snapshot of changes, with a short message describing what changed and why. Think "save point," not just "save file." Push Sending your commits from your computer up to GitHub. Pull Downloading the latest commits from GitHub down to your computer. Branch A parallel, independent copy of the repo's files where you can make changes without affecting the main version. Useful for trying something without risk. Main branch The default, "official" branch — usually the version considered finished/current. Most repos just use this one branch. Pull request (PR) A request to merge changes from a branch into main, so others can review before it becomes official. Merge Combining changes from one branch into another (e.g., a PR being accepted into main). Issue A tracked to-do item, bug report, or question attached to a repo — a lightweight way to flag something without emailing. README The first file people see when opening a repo — usually a short explanation of what it is and how to use it. Template repo A pre-built repo structure (like repo-template) you copy to start a new project with the right folders already in place. Fork Your own independent copy of someone else's repo — rarely needed inside this org, more common for outside/public projects.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: You don't need to understand all of this to contribute — filling out repo-manifest.yml and docs/index.md in a repo created from repo-template only needs: edit a file, save, commit, push. See the organization contributing guide or ask the organization admin.

docs.title: HemgenixCEA
docs.text: Cost-effectiveness analysis of Hemgenix (etranacogene dezaparvovec) versus Alprolix (eftrenonacog alfa) for hemophilia B in Canada.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Markov cohort model comparing a one-time gene therapy (Hemgenix) against extended half-life FIX prophylaxis (Alprolix) over a lifetime horizon. Built in R, structured around weekly cycles, and calibrated to Canadian epidemiology and costs.

Indication: Hemophilia B (FIX deficiency) Perspective: Canadian health system Horizon: Lifetime (~59 years, 3 077 weekly cycles) Discount rate: 1.5% for costs and effects

docs.title: Model Structure
docs.text:
Four health states:

State Description No_bleed Alive, bleed-free JB Joint bleed (4-day duration) NJB Non-joint bleed (2-day duration) Death Absorbing

Background mortality drawn from Statistics Canada life tables (2022, both sexes). Transitions are cycle-varying — death probability updated each cycle from age at entry.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• R ≥ 4.2
  • Packages: tidyverse, readxl, dampack

Install packages:

install.packages(c("tidyverse", "readxl", "dampack"))

docs.title: Running the Analysis
docs.text:
Step 1 — Prepare mortality data (only needed once, or when updating the life table):

source("bg_mortality.R")   # writes df_mortality.rds

Step 2 — Knit the main analysis:

rmarkdown::render("analysis.Rmd")

Output: analysis.html

docs.title: Repository Structure
docs.text:
HemgenixCEA/
├── analysis.Rmd            # main model and results
├── bg_mortality.R          # mortality data prep
├── mortality_testing.R     # mortality model tests
├── mortality_testing_v2.R  # mortality model tests (v2)
├── utilities.xlsx          # AE disutilities and durations
├── db_all_mortality.csv    # Statistics Canada life table (raw)
├── db_all_mortality.xlsx   # same, Excel copy
├── df_mortality.rds        # processed mortality lookup
├── ED_mat_trans.RDS        # pre-computed Hemgenix transition matrix
├── debugging.xlsx          # scratch / validation workbook
├── repo-manifest.yml       # machine-readable repo metadata
└── docs/
    └── index.md            # this file

docs.title: RShiny SEE Scaffold — Haemophilia A
docs.text: Configurable RShiny scaffold for MRC-compliant Structured Expert Elicitation (SEE). Clone, edit one file, deploy.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This scaffold lets researchers run a web-based Structured Expert Elicitation study without writing R code. Experts access a hosted Shiny app, work through guided probability elicitation questions (Chips & Bins, Quartiles, or Tertiles), and save their responses as CSV files.

The first deployed use case elicits expert opinion on the probability of joint surgery at multiple HJHS (Haemophilia Joint Health Score) cutpoints. The scaffold is study-agnostic: all study content lives in manual_inputs.R and the www/ HTML fragments.

Design follows the STEER protocol (Supporting The Elicitation of Expert knowledge in R) and the Bojke et al. (2022) MRC SEE guidelines.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• R 4.0+
  • RStudio (recommended)
  • Internet connection on first run (packages auto-install)

R packages installed automatically by app.R:

Package Purpose shiny Web app framework bslib Bootstrap 5 theming shinydashboard Dashboard layout rdrop2 Dropbox integration (v2) SHELF Distribution fitting (analysis scripts)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/GitHEE-UMCU/haemophilia-see.git

# Open haemophilia-see.Rproj in RStudio
# Packages install automatically on first app launch

docs.title: Running Locally
docs.text:
# In RStudio: open app.R and click Run App
# Or from terminal:
Rscript app.R

Set dummy_app <- TRUE in app.R for local testing (bypasses expert ID gating).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All study-specific content lives in manual_inputs.R. Edit this file only — no changes to ui.R or server.R needed.

Key parameters:

Parameter What it controls all_expert_ids Allowed expert ID codes elicitation_method "chips and bins", "quartiles", or "tertiles" quantity One entry per elicitation question eli_que_text Full question text shown to experts quant_limit_lower/upper Numeric bounds per quantity conditional_release TRUE locks tab progression in production save_method "local" (CSV download) or "dropbox"

HTML content (welcome, background, instructions, consent) lives in www/*.htm — edit these as plain HTML fragments.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy to shinyapps.io:

# Install rsconnect if needed
install.packages("rsconnect")

# Connect account via RStudio Tools > Global Options > Publishing
# Then deploy:
rsconnect::deployApp()

Before deploying: set dummy_app <- FALSE and conditional_release <- TRUE in manual_inputs.R.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
app.R                  Entry point
manual_inputs.R        ALL study config — edit this
ui.R                   Tab layout (reads manual_inputs.R)
server.R               App logic (reads manual_inputs.R)
www/
  text_home.htm
  text_background_info.htm
  text_instructions_*.htm
  text_consent.htm
analysis_files/        Expert response CSVs saved here
STEER-main/            Reference implementation (read-only)

docs.title: Reusing for a New Study
docs.text:
1. Clone or fork this repo
  2. Edit manual_inputs.R — IDs, questions, units, limits, elicitation method
  3. Edit www/ HTML fragments — welcome, background, instructions
  4. Test locally with dummy_app = TRUE
  5. Deploy to shinyapps.io with dummy_app = FALSE

docs.title: Microsimulation Model for Hemophilia A (DosEmi)
docs.text: Individual-level microsimulation for cost-effectiveness analysis of PK-guided emicizumab dosing vs. standard-of-care in hemophilia A patients.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This model simulates hemophilia A patients from the DosEmi study over time, tracking joint health (HJHS scores), bleeds, costs, and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs). It compares two treatment strategies:

  • SOC — standard-of-care emicizumab dosing
  • PK — pharmacokinetic-guided (individualized) emicizumab dosing

Patients can switch from PK to SOC if bleeding thresholds are exceeded within a 6-month window.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• R (≥ 4.0)
  • Packages: tidyverse, dplyr, tidyr
  • Input data: data/dosemi.RData, data/DosEmi_data_clean.RData, data/df_PK_df_pros_fixed.RData

docs.title: Running the Model
docs.text:
# 1. Process data
source("01_data_process.R")

# 2. Load helper functions
source("02_functions.R")

# 3. Run microsimulation
source("03_microsimulation.R")

# 4. Analyse results (RMarkdown)
rmarkdown::render("04_analysis.Rmd")

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
Individual-level microsimulation comparing PK-guided vs. standard-of-care emicizumab dosing in hemophilia A. Monthly cycles; each patient tracked independently.

dosemi.RData
    │
    ▼
01_data_process.R   ── pivot to long format, complete cases
    │
    ▼
02_functions.R      ── ProbsBleeds / Costs / Effs helpers
    │
    ▼
03_microsimulation.R ── run_microsim() main loop
    │
    ▼
04_analysis.Rmd     ── results, tables, PSA/DSA

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text: Component Description 01_data_process.R Loads dosemi.RData, filters complete cases, reshapes to long format (SOC vs. PK columns → rows) 02_functions.R ProbsBleeds() — negative-binomial bleed draw, HJHS update, state classification; Costs() — prophylaxis, bleed treatment, acute care, societal costs; Effs() — QALY calculation with HJHS/bleed/injection disutilities 03_microsimulation.R run_microsim() — patient-month nested loop, surgery events, treatment switching, mortality, discounting, trace matrix 04_analysis.Rmd Aggregates outputs, ICER calculation, sensitivity analyses

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Input: patient-level DosEmi study data (HJHS, ABR, utility, dosing by treatment arm)
  2. Data processing: complete-case filter → long format with life factor (SOC/PK)
  3. Simulation: for each patient × month — draw bleeds (neg-binomial), update HJHS score, classify state (A/B/C/D), apply surgery probability, compute costs and QALYs, check mortality, apply switching rule
  4. Output: discounted total costs (tc), QALYs (te), state trace matrix (TR), transition strings (TS)

docs.title: HJHS States
docs.text: State HJHS Score A < 15 (mild) B 15–24 C 25–34 D ≥ 35 (severe)

docs.title: Treatment Switching Rule
docs.text: Patient on PK switches to SOC if, in any rolling 6-month window: - ≥ 1 spontaneous joint/muscle bleed, or - > 2 traumatic joint/muscle bleeds

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Dependency Purpose tidyverse / tidyr Data reshaping in 01_data_process.R dplyr Data manipulation Base R rnbinom, rbinom for stochastic draws

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text: Local R analysis — no cloud deployment. Data files stored in data/ (excluded from git via .gitignore).

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text: Decision Rationale Individual-level (microsimulation) over cohort Markov Captures heterogeneity in PK parameters and baseline HJHS across patients Negative-binomial bleed distribution Accounts for overdispersion in bleed counts observed in DosEmi data Monthly cycle length Matches emicizumab dosing intervals and clinical follow-up frequency Complete-case analysis Simplifies initial implementation; multiple imputation planned

docs.text:
